title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 108
paragraphs: So Hippias concluded that his dream had been thus fulfilled. Meanwhile the Athenians, drawn up in the sacred precinct of Heracles, were joined by the Plataeans, who came to their aid in full force. For the Plataeans had given themselves to the Athenians, and the Athenians had undertaken many labors on their behalf. The surrender had come about like this. Being oppressed by the Thebans, the Plataeans had first tried to give themselves to Cleomenes son of Anaxandridas and to the Lacedaemonians, who happened to be in the area. But the Lacedaemonians would not accept them and said: “We live too far off, and our help to you would be cold comfort. You might be enslaved many times over before any of us heard of it. We advise you instead to give yourselves to the Athenians — they are your neighbors, and they are no bad allies.” The Lacedaemonians gave this advice not so much out of goodwill for the Plataeans as out of a wish that the Athenians should be caught up in trouble and conflict with the Boeotians. The Plataeans did not fail to follow the counsel. While the Athenians were offering sacrifice to the twelve gods, the Plataeans seated themselves as suppliants at the altar and so handed themselves over. When the Thebans learned of this, they marched against the Plataeans, and the Athenians came to their defense. Just as the two sides were about to join battle, the Corinthians, who happened to be there, would not allow them to fight but reconciled the quarrel. Both parties put the matter in their hands, and the Corinthians fixed the boundaries of the land on the condition that the Thebans should leave alone any Boeotians who did not wish to be counted among them. After this decision the Corinthians departed. But as the Athenians were withdrawing, the Boeotians attacked them, and in the resulting battle were defeated. The Athenians then advanced beyond the boundaries the Corinthians had set for the Plataeans and made the river Asopus itself the border between Thebes and the territory of Plataea and Hysiae. That is how the Plataeans had given themselves to the Athenians, and now they had come to Marathon to bring them support.
